nodes.label: In-model essentiality can only live in explicitly wired machinery: the classi...
nodes.statement: In-model essentiality can only live in explicitly wired machinery: the classification scan for this panel found tufA (EF-Tu), fusA (EF-G), infC (IF-3), and ftsZ are expression-only - no functional wiring in complexation, metabolism, regulation, two-component, equilibrium, or any functional molecule group - so knocking out these biologically essential genes would read as inert. Conversely dnaG, which a complexation-only scan misses, is directly consumed as a replisome monomer subunit.

nodes.label: A ParCa-level knockout of ANY ppGpp-regulated gene crashes the build at step ...
nodes.statement: A ParCa-level knockout of ANY ppGpp-regulated gene crashes the build at step 3: set_ppgpp_expression (transcription.py:1935) indexes its fold-change table by cistron id, the deleted gene's cistron has left the functional index, and the lookup raises KeyError('<gene>_RNA'). 393 genes (~8% of the genome) are in ppgpp_regulated_genes, so this is the blast radius. The class-C "essentiality" signal is entirely preempted by this crash - cspA (class A: functionally unwired, biologically dispensable at 37C) fails identically to rpoB/rplB/dnaG, proving the failure is regulon membership, not essentiality. This is the first FATAL instance of the D17 dangling-reference class (the generator prunes nothing by design; consequences are this investigation's subject matter), and what "essential machinery" would do in the model remains unobserved.

nodes.label: Identical failure tails for cspA, rpoB, rplB, dnaG (KeyError on EG10166_RNA /...
nodes.statement: Identical failure tails for cspA, rpoB, rplB, dnaG (KeyError on EG10166_RNA / EG10894_RNA / EG10865_RNA / EG10239_RNA respectively); --allow-partial-fit does not help (the crash precedes the fit). len(ppgpp_regulated_genes) = 393 (8.7% of the 4538 functional cistrons; 4747 raw genes would give 8.3% - the cistron set is the one set_ppgpp_expression indexes, so it is the operative denominator). Crash-vs-regulon-membership agrees 8/8 with ZERO mismatches across the panel. Committed backing: data/evidence.json E-1, regenerated by sims/extract_evidence.py.

nodes.label: The refit artifact for a functionally-inert knockout has a clean three-part s...
nodes.statement: The refit artifact for a functionally-inert knockout has a clean three-part structure: (a) a per-mille bulk shift (median relative expression delta 0.02-0.16% across the four builders, scaling with the deleted gene's freed expression share), (b) ~10-12% shifts confined to the deleted gene's OPERON NEIGHBORS (ygiB's tail is ygiC and tolC - transcription-unit share reattribution after TU truncation), and (c) large relative deltas on numerically-zero cistrons (1e-24-scale expression) that mean nothing. The wired-but-nonessential class (pgi, tpiA - genes with real growth defects) is barely distinguishable from a chemotaxis gene at the expression level, consistent with the expectation that the model under-reacts to their loss.

nodes.label: expression_delta_vs_wt in data/panel_summary.json: ygiB median 2.1e-4 / pgi 9...
nodes.statement: expression_delta_vs_wt in data/panel_summary.json: ygiB median 2.1e-4 / pgi 9.2e-4 / tpiA 1.6e-3 / cheY 8.2e-4; >5% tails 0.1-0.3% of cistrons; ygiB's >5% tail is 9 cistrons, of which exactly 2 carry real expression: ygiC (EG11165_RNA) and tolC (EG11009_RNA), both at 12.35%; the other 7 sit below a 1e-12 zero floor and their relative deltas are meaningless. Committed backing: data/evidence.json E-2, regenerated by sims/extract_evidence.py.

nodes.label: v2ecoli's transcriptional-regulatory network covers 2198 of 4347 mRNA cistron...
nodes.statement: v2ecoli's transcriptional-regulatory network covers 2198 of 4347 mRNA cistrons - 50.6%. It is 4209 edges from 150 transcription factors onto 2231 distinct target names. ⛔ An earlier version of this finding reported 663 of 4347 (15.2%) from 47 TFs; that was measured from fold_changes.tsv ALONE and was wrong - see the correction note below.

nodes.label: Both fold-change tables merged as the loader merges them (simulation_data.py:...
nodes.statement: Both fold-change tables merged as the loader merges them (simulation_data.py:191 iterates ["fold_changes", "fold_changes_nca"], NCA second so it wins on overlap), minus fold_changes_removed.tsv: 4209 edges, 150 TFs, 2231 distinct targets, 2198 of which resolve to mRNA cistrons out of 4347. Re-derivable via sims/extract_evidence.py.

nodes.label: The model's trpR regulon is 12 edges and covers ALL FIVE of EcoCyc's TrpR ope...
nodes.statement: The model's trpR regulon is 12 edges and covers ALL FIVE of EcoCyc's TrpR operator regions - trpLEDCBA, aroH, aroL, mtr, and trpR's own negative autoregulation - plus aroM and yaiA. ⛔ An earlier version of this finding claimed 7 edges over 2 of 5 regions, and that aroL, mtr and trpR carried no regulatory edge from any transcription factor. That was wrong in both halves; all three are repressed by trpR in the table the model actually loads.

nodes.label: Effective trpR targets after merging both tables and applying fold_changes_re...
nodes.statement: Effective trpR targets after merging both tables and applying fold_changes_removed: yaiA 4.03x, trpA 3.94x, trpC 3.89x, mtr 3.89x, trpB 3.78x, trpR 3.73x, trpD 3.71x, trpL 3.68x, aroH 3.46x, trpE 3.41x, aroM 2.77x, aroL 2.62x. The NCA table supplies aroL, aroM, mtr, trpR and yaiA, and overwrites all seven shared targets.

nodes.label: In the model's parameter tables the control hierarchy is INVERTED against the...
nodes.statement: In the model's parameter tables the control hierarchy is INVERTED against the literature. TrpR repression terms are 2.62-4.03x where the literature reports 70-300x, while attenuation terms on the same operon are 5.98-7.36x against a literature 8-10x. On all 5 genes where both mechanisms act, the model's attenuation term is LARGER than its repression term - the opposite of the documented ordering.

nodes.label: Per shared target, TrpR repression vs attenuation (fold), using the effective...
nodes.statement: Per shared target, TrpR repression vs attenuation (fold), using the effective merged table: trpA 3.94 vs 7.36, trpB 3.78 vs 6.96, trpC 3.89 vs 7.16, trpD 3.71 vs 6.68, trpE 3.41 vs 5.98. Repression exceeds attenuation on 0 of 5.

nodes.label: tRNA transcriptional attenuation is OFF in a default v2ecoli run. The attenua...
nodes.statement: tRNA transcriptional attenuation is OFF in a default v2ecoli run. The attenuation terms F-03 measures are present in the shipped tables but inactive unless explicitly enabled, so in a default simulation trp control rests on the TrpR term alone.

nodes.label: Route A - chromosomal deletion of trpR before reconstruction - does not build...
nodes.statement: Route A - chromosomal deletion of trpR before reconstruction - does not build. Both the trpR single and the trpR+tnaA double fail ParCa at step 9 with an identical ValueError on the amino-acid homeostasis check for TRP[c]. This is a third knockout failure class, distinct from the fatal dangling reference of the ppGpp path and from silent target-side drops: a validated invariant tripping loudly, which is arguably the system working.

Genotype ids 0adf8b53af80154d (trpR, EG11029) and 70d3080e93e991f3 (trpRtnaA, EG11029+EG11005). Artifact: data/route_a_summary.json.

nodes.label: The route-A failure cleanly separates BUILD INTEGRITY from PARAMETER FITTING....
nodes.statement: The route-A failure cleanly separates BUILD INTEGRITY from PARAMETER FITTING. All six structural axes pass within tolerance on both arms - chromosome length, round-trip, coordinate bounds, coordinate shift, tombstone, and functional absence - so the genome splice is sound and the genotype is well-formed. It is ParCa's fit, not the deletion machinery, that rejects it.

nodes.label: The model's TrpR regulation WORKS, and the earlier basal null result was corr...
nodes.statement: The model's TrpR regulation WORKS, and the earlier basal null result was correct behaviour rather than a divergence. Removing TrpR in the condition where the model declares it active derepresses the trp operon 6.29x; in basal, where the model declares it inactive, the same knockout changes nothing (1.06x). The knockout itself is total in both - zero TrpR copies against 42-80 in the matched wild type.

nodes.label: Time-mean trp TU (TU00067) synthesis probability, second-half window, 3 gener...
nodes.statement: Time-mean trp TU (TU00067) synthesis probability, second-half window, 3 generations, seed 0. AA-replete: WT 6.63e-05, trpR KO 4.17e-04, ratio 6.29x. Basal: WT 5.77e-04, trpR KO 6.14e-04, ratio 1.06x. TrpR monomer: 0 in every KO sample, 42-80 in WT. Fraction of samples with the operon repressed (<1e-8): AA-replete WT 74%, KO 0%. Artifacts: data/route_b_*.json.

nodes.label: The measured derepression (6.29x) is the same order as the ceiling predicted ...
nodes.statement: The measured derepression (6.29x) is the same order as the ceiling predicted statically from the model's own merged fold-change table (F-02/F-03: 2.62-4.03x), though somewhat above it - the readout is transcription-unit level while the terms are per-target, so they are related but not the same quantity and exact agreement was not expected. Two independent methods - reading the shipped parameter table, and running the knockout - agree. So B1's predicted failure against the literature's 70-300x is a parameterization result, fully accounted for, and not a defect in the knockout machinery or the run.

nodes.label: Static (F-02/F-03, both tables merged as the loader merges them): TrpR terms ...
nodes.statement: Static (F-02/F-03, both tables merged as the loader merges them): TrpR terms 2.62-4.03x. Dynamic (F-07, from the run): 6.29x. Literature: 70-300x.
